questions.text: Separate the real and imaginary parts of $(\sqrt{2}+i)^{-2}$.
Find the real and imaginary parts of $(1-\sqrt{5}i)^{-1}$.
Solve the complex equation $(x,y)(2,3)=(-4,7)$.
Find the real and imaginary parts of $\left(\frac{1-i}{2-i}\right)^{-1}$.
Solve $z^2-4z+5=0$ by completing the square, where $z$ is a complex number.

Using properties of determinants, prove that $\begin{vmatrix}\alpha&\beta\gamma&\alpha\beta\gamma\\\beta&\gamma\alpha&\alpha\beta\gamma\\\gamma&\alpha\beta&\alpha\beta\gamma\end{vmatrix}=\begin{vmatrix}\alpha&\alpha^2&\alpha^3\\\beta&\beta^2&\beta^3\\\gamma&\gamma^2&\gamma^3\end{vmatrix}$.
Show that $\begin{bmatrix}1&-2&-6\\-3&2&9\\2&0&-3\end{bmatrix}$ is a periodic matrix of period $2$.
Using properties of determinants, show that $\begin{vmatrix}1&x&y+z\\1&y&z+x\\1&z&x+y\end{vmatrix}=0$.
Find the rank of $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\2&3&4\\0&2&2\end{bmatrix}$ using elementary row operations.
If $A=\begin{bmatrix}-2&1&0\\-1&4&3\\0&0&5\end{bmatrix}$, find $A^2-5A+4I$.
Using properties of determinants, prove that $\begin{vmatrix}b+c&a&a\\b&c+a&b\\c&c&a+b\end{vmatrix}=4abc$.
Show that $A=\begin{bmatrix}-5&-8&0\\3&5&0\\1&2&-1\end{bmatrix}$ is an involutory matrix.
Without expanding, show that $\begin{vmatrix}x+1&x+3&x+5\\x+4&x+6&x+8\\x+7&x+9&x+11\end{vmatrix}=0$.
Find the real numbers $x,y,z$ such that $A$ is Hermitian, where $A=\begin{bmatrix}3&x+2i&yi\\3-2i&0&1+zi\\yi&i-xi&-1\end{bmatrix}$.

Without expanding determinants, prove that $\begin{vmatrix}\alpha&\beta\gamma&\alpha\beta\gamma\\\beta&\gamma\alpha&\alpha\beta\gamma\\\gamma&\alpha\beta&\alpha\beta\gamma\end{vmatrix}=\begin{vmatrix}\alpha&\alpha^2&\alpha^3\\\beta&\beta^2&\beta^3\\\gamma&\gamma^2&\gamma^3\end{vmatrix}$.
Use the Gauss–Jordan method to solve the system $x-y+4z=4$, $2x+2y-z=2$, $3x-2y+3z=-3$.
Use the Gauss–Jordan method to solve the system $x+5y+2z=9$, $x+y+7z=6$, $-3y+4z=-2$.
Solve the non-homogeneous system using Gaussian elimination: $-x+y+z=0$, $x+2y=1$, $-3x+2y-z=-2$.
Use the Gauss–Jordan method to solve the system $2x+2y-z=4$, $x-2y+z=2$, $x+y=0$.
Use the Gauss–Jordan method to solve the non-homogeneous system $x-y+4z=4$, $2x+2y-z=2$, $3x-2y+3z=-3$.
Find the angle between the vectors $3\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$ and $\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+\hat{k}$.
Find $\lambda$ if the vectors $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $\lambda\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, and $3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ are coplanar.
Calculate the projection of $\vec b$ along $\vec a$ when $\vec a=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $\vec b=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$.
If $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ are the direction angles of a vector, show that $\sin^2\alpha+\sin^2\beta+\sin^2\gamma=2$.
Find $\lambda$ if the vectors $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $\lambda\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, and $3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ are coplanar.
In parallelogram $ABCD$, $X$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and $Y$ divides $BC$ in the ratio $1:2$. Show that if $Z$ divides $DX$ in the ratio $6:1$, then it also divides $AY$ in the ratio $3:4$.
Points $A,B,C$ have position vectors $\vec a,\vec b,2\vec a-\vec b$, respectively. Point $D$ divides $AC$ in the ratio $2:3$, and $E$ divides $BD$ in the ratio $4:1$. Find the position vector of $E$.
Find the volume of the tetrahedron with vertices $A(2,1,8)$, $B(3,2,9)$, $C(2,1,4)$, and $D(3,3,10)$.
Prove the hexagon law of vector addition.
The points $A(1,1)$, $B(5,4)$, $C(8,9)$, and $D(0,3)$ represent position vectors. Show that $ABCD$ is a trapezium.
Points $A,B,C$ have position vectors $\vec a,\vec b,2\vec a-\vec b$, respectively. Point $D$ divides $AC$ in the ratio $2:3$, and $E$ divides $BD$ in the ratio $4:1$. Find the position vector of $E$.
Insert three arithmetic means between $3$ and $11$.
In a G.P., $a_3=12$ and $a_8=384$. Find the $n^{\text{th}}$ term.
Find the $13^{\text{th}}$ term of an A.P. whose first term and common difference are $3$ and $-4$, respectively. Also write its first four terms.
Find the $8^{\text{th}}$ term of the H.P. $\frac45,\frac25,\frac4{15},\ldots$.
Find the arithmetic, geometric, and harmonic means between $1$ and $9$. Also verify that $AH=G^2$.
Find three consecutive numbers in G.P. whose sum is $39$ and product is $729$.
Find $n$ so that $\frac{x^{n+5}+y^{n+5}}{x^{n+4}+y^{n+4}}$ may be the arithmetic mean between $x$ and $y$.
If the $3^{\text{rd}}$ and $7^{\text{th}}$ terms of an H.P. are $\frac29$ and $\frac2{25}$, respectively, find the sequence.
If the $p^{\text{th}}$ term of an H.P. is $q$ and the $q^{\text{th}}$ term is $p$, prove that the $(p+q)^{\text{th}}$ term is $\frac{pq}{p+q}$.
Find $\displaystyle\sum_{k=2}^{\infty}\frac{1}{k^2-1}$.
Find $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{4k^2-1}$.
Find the sum to $n$ terms of $3+6+21+96+471+\cdots$.
Find the sum of $1+2\cdot5+3\cdot5^2+4\cdot5^3+\cdots$ to $30$ terms.
Find the sum to $n$ terms of $3+6+15+42+123+\cdots$.
There are $11$ men and $9$ women in a club. How many committees of $8$ members can be formed with exactly five men?
How many words can be formed using $3$ vowels and $4$ consonants chosen from $5$ vowels and $7$ consonants?
How many arrangements can be formed using all the letters of the word “MATHEMATICS”?
How many distinct permutations of the letters of the word “ESSENTIAL” are possible?
In how many ways can two English books, three chemistry books, and four physics books be arranged on a shelf so that all books of the same subject remain together?
For events $A$ and $B$, $P(A)=\frac14$, $P(A^{\prime}\mid B)=\frac12$, and $P(B\mid A)=\frac23$. Find $P(A\cap B)$ and $P(B)$.
The king, queen, and jack of clubs are removed from a deck of $52$ playing cards, and the remaining cards are shuffled. One card is drawn. Find the probabilities.
In a three-child family, find the probabilities.
The king, queen, and jack of clubs are removed from a deck of $52$ playing cards, and the remaining cards are shuffled. One card is drawn. Find the probabilities.
A room has $3$ lamps selected at random from $10$ light bulbs, of which $6$ are good. The bulbs are put into the sockets. What is the probability that the room will light?
Using mathematical induction, prove that $7^n-4^n$ is divisible by $3$.
Using mathematical induction, prove that $1^3+2^3+3^3+\cdots+n^3=\left(\frac{n(n+1)}2\right)^2$ for every natural number $n$.
Using mathematical induction, prove that $2+4+6+\cdots+2n=n(n+1)$ for every $n\in\mathbb N$.
For every positive integer $n$, prove that $\frac1{1\cdot2}+\frac1{2\cdot3}+\frac1{3\cdot4}+\cdots+\frac1{n(n+1)}=\frac{n}{n+1}$.
Find the middle term in the expansion of $\left(\frac ab-\frac ba\right)^{18}$.
Find the term independent of $x$ in $\left(2x+\frac1{x^2}\right)^9$.
Using mathematical induction, prove that $1+4+7+\cdots+(3n-2)=\frac{n(3n-1)}2$ for every positive integer $n$.
Use the binomial theorem to find $(19)^4$.
Using mathematical induction, prove that $2+4+6+\cdots+2n=n(n+1)$ for every positive integer $n$.
Write in simplified form the term independent of $x$ in $\left(2x+\frac1{x^2}\right)^9$.
If $x=\frac13+\frac{1\cdot3}{3\cdot6}+\frac{1\cdot3\cdot5}{3\cdot6\cdot9}+\cdots$, prove that $x^2+2x-2=0$.
Use the binomial theorem to show that $1+\frac14+\frac{1(-3)}{4\cdot6}+\frac{1(-3)(-5)}{4\cdot6\cdot8}+\cdots=\sqrt[4]{4}$.
Use the binomial theorem to show that $4x^2-2x-1=0$ if $\frac1x=\frac25+\frac{1\cdot3}{2!}\left(\frac25\right)^2+\frac{1\cdot3\cdot5}{3!}\left(\frac25\right)^3+\cdots$.
If $\frac1x=\frac25+\frac{1\cdot3}{2!}\left(\frac25\right)^2+\frac{1\cdot3\cdot5}{3!}\left(\frac25\right)^3+\cdots$, show that $4x^2-2x-1=0$.
Find the inverse of $f$ and determine the domain and range of $f^{-1}$ for $f(x)=\frac{x-1}{x-3}$, $x\ne3$.
Find and verify the inverse of the real-valued function $f(x)=5x+7$.
Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be defined by $f(x)=\sqrt{x+7}$ for $x\ge-7$. Find $f^{-1}(x)$.
Find graphically the point of intersection of $f(x)=x+4$ and $g(x)=x^2-6x+10$.
Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be defined by $f(x)=-5x+1$. Find $f^{-1}(0)$.
Find the equation of a quadratic graph $y=ax^2+bx+c$ that crosses the $x$-axis at $(-4,0)$ and $(3,0)$ and passes through $(2,-4)$.
Find graphically the point of intersection of $f(x)=x+4$ and $g(x)=x^2-6x+10$.
Find graphically the points of intersection of $y=2x+1$ and $y=x^2-4x+6$, for $x\in\mathbb R$.
Find graphically the points of intersection of $y=f(x)=2x+1$ and $y=g(x)=x^2-4x+6$, for $x\in\mathbb R$.
If $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is defined by $f(x)=5x+7$, find $f^{-1}(x)$ and verify that $f^{-1}(f(x))=x$.
Solve graphically: for $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$, maximize $Z(x,y)=10x+11y$ subject to $2x+3y\le8$ and $6x+3y\le10$.
Solve graphically: for $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$, maximize $Z(x,y)=30x+36y$ subject to $4x+2y\le12$ and $6x+5y\le20$.
Solve the linear-programming problem: for $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$, maximize $Z(x,y)=30x+36y$ subject to $4x+2y\le12$ and $6x+5y\le20$.
